entries.title: Job 39:1
segments: ¶Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? [or] canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

entries.title: Job 39:2
segments: Canst thou number the months [that] they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

entries.title: Job 39:3
segments: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.

entries.title: Job 39:4
segments: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.

entries.title: Job 39:5
segments: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?

entries.title: Job 39:6
segments: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings. {barren...: Heb. salt places}

entries.title: Job 39:7
segments: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver. {of the driver: Heb. of the exactor}

words.text: . {of the driver: Heb. of the exactor}

entries.title: Job 39:8
segments: The range of the mountains [is] his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

entries.title: Job 39:9
segments: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?

entries.title: Job 39:10
segments: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

entries.title: Job 39:11
segments: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength [is] great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

entries.title: Job 39:12
segments: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather [it into] thy barn?

words.text: him, that he will bring home

entries.title: Job 39:13
segments: ¶[Gavest thou] the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich? {wings and...: or, the feathers of the stork and ostrich}

words.text: ? {wings and...: or, the feathers of the stork and ostrich}

entries.title: Job 39:14
segments: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,

entries.title: Job 39:15
segments: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.

entries.title: Job 39:16
segments: She is hardened against her young ones, as though [they were] not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

entries.title: Job 39:17
segments: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

entries.title: Job 39:18
segments: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.

entries.title: Job 39:19
segments: ¶Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?

entries.title: Job 39:20
segments: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils [is] terrible. {terrible: Heb. terror}

entries.title: Job 39:21
segments: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in [his] strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men. {He paweth: or, His feet dig} {the armed...: Heb. the armour}

words.text: . {He paweth: or, His feet dig} {the armed...: Heb. the armour}

entries.title: Job 39:22
segments: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.

entries.title: Job 39:23
segments: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.

entries.title: Job 39:24
segments: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that [it is] the sound of the trumpet.

entries.title: Job 39:25
segments: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

entries.title: Job 39:26
segments: ¶Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, [and] stretch her wings toward the south?

entries.title: Job 39:27
segments: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high? {at...: Heb. by thy mouth}

entries.title: Job 39:28
segments: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.

entries.title: Job 39:29
segments: From thence she seeketh the prey, [and] her eyes behold afar off.

entries.title: Job 39:30
segments: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain [are], there [is] she.
